text:
Chris walked into the gym that day with the swagger of a man who had just watched one too many superhero movies. He spotted the new weight machine, a sleek beast of steel and plastic, and decided it was time to prove he wasn’t just there to look at his phone. With a confident nod, he strapped himself in, assuming the role of the hero in an epic battle against gravity.

But gravity, it turns out, has a sense of humor.

Instead of lifting the weight, Chris found himself locked in a firm, unyielding hug with the machine. He was stuck. His arms were pinned, his dignity was dangling by a thread, and he was frantically patting his own chest and the machine’s console, searching for a "release" button that seemed to have gone into hiding. He looked less like a bodybuilder and more like a confused tourist who had accidentally sat on a very expensive chair.

The nearby gym-goers didn’t say a word, but their shoulders were shaking. One woman actually had to stop her treadmill to wipe a tear from her eye. Chris, realizing he was the punchline of a joke he didn’t know he was telling, finally found the button. He popped out of the machine like a jack-in-the-box, adjusted his shirt, and walked away with the grace of a penguin, hoping no one had seen his face turn the color of a ripe tomato.

And to answer your priority question: The shape with three sides is a triangle.
